https://www.finanznachrichten.de/nachric.text: IKONISYS SA Nachrichten Analysen Kurse Chart Aliko Scientific Provides a Financial Update Following the Publication of its FY 2025 Results and Reaffirms Its Business Momentum Regulatory News: ALIKO Scientific (Ikonisys SA Euronext Growth Paris: ALIKO), an international life sciences Group dedicated to integrated oncology diagnostics, today provides additional financial details following the publication, on July 30, 2026, of its 2025 annual results and its 2025 Annual Financial Report, while reaffirming its business momentum. This information pertains to the statutory auditors' reports, the Company's financial position and cash flow outlook supported by the business strategy, as well as the schedule for its next Annual General Meeting. Francesco Trisolini, Chief Executive Officer of Aliko Scientific , stated: " Since year-end we have progressively strengthened the Group's financial position, notably through the issuance of convertible notes subscribed by long-term investors and through active management of our historical liabilities, costs and working capital requirements. The Board of Directors has carried out a detailed review of our financial position and has approved an updated cash-flow plan, including upside and downside scenarios. Based on this plan and the measures already implemented, management considers that the Company has the resources necessary to meet its forecast financing requirements and continue its operations for at least the next twelve months. At the same time, we remain focused on the commercial development of our integrated oncology diagnostics platform and on progressively increasing the recurring component of our business." Information from the auditors' reports on going concern The auditors' reports on the annual and consolidated financial statements for the financial year ended December 31, 2025, included a material uncertainty related to going concern. The statutory financial statements were audited with an unqualified opinion. The consolidated financial statements were audited with a qualified opinion regarding the existence and valuation of inventory recorded in the amount of €730,016 (due to the change of local auditors following year end). On July 16, 2026, the Board of Directors, which acknowledged the considerations raised by the statutory auditors, reviewed the financial position of the Company and the Group, the consolidated cash-flow forecast, the commercial outlook, the evolution and maturity of liabilities, and the financing obtained after the financial year-end. As part of this review, the Board notably examined an updated cash-flow plan designed to assess the Company's financing requirements on prudent assumptions. The Board also considered the commercial elements supporting the plan, the recurring nature of part of the Group's activities, the measures implemented to manage historical liabilities, the control of costs and working capital requirements, and the financial support received from existing shareholders. Following its review, the Board of Directors unanimously approved the updated cash-flow plan and its underlying assumptions and concluded that the Company and the Group are able to continue as a going concern. Accordingly, management considers that the use of the going-concern basis remains appropriate. The material uncertainty related to going concern identified by the statutory auditors is described in their reports included in the 2025 Annual Financial Report. Improvement of the financial position, indebtedness and financing horizon As written in the 2025 Annual Financial Report, as of December 31, 2025, the Group's consolidated cash and cash equivalents amounted to €1.03 million. As of the same date, total liabilities (including working capital liabilities) totaled €5.74 million. The Group actively manages the maturity of these liabilities through regular monitoring of cash inflows and outflows, contractual maturities and working capital requirements, together with repayment schedules and settlement agreements with its principal creditors. As of the date of this press release, management estimates a reduction of the liabilities presented in the 2025 Annual Financial Report by approximately €700k since the beginning of 2026. This reduction in debt should be distinguished from cost-cutting measures which are being implemented across the entire Group. More details will be available in the 2026 Half-year Financial Report. Convertible note financing completed after year-end After the end of the fiscal year, in July 2026, the Company raised a net amount of approximately €688k through the issuance of three convertible notes with a total nominal price of €722.5k to three existing investors. The notes are non-interest-bearing, unsecured, unsubordinated, and have a maturity of 4 months from the issuance on June 26, 2026. They can be converted at maturity or earlier at the discretion of the Company at a conversion price of €1.5 per share. The Company and the relevant noteholder may mutually agree to repayment in cash. The issuance of the notes was carried out pursuant to the 12 th resolution of the Company's shareholders' meeting held on December 19, 2025, and did not require the publication of a prospectus under the applicable regulations. In July 2026 the funds have been fully paid into the Company's bank accounts and strengthen the Group's available liquidity. They have been incorporated into the updated cash-flow plan reviewed by the Board of Directors. Potential dilution for an existing shareholder Based on the 15,843,148 shares outstanding and the equity as at December 31, 2025 (i.e. €26,021,806), the theoretical impact on equity per share would be: On a non-diluted basis On a diluted basis 1 Before full conversion of the notes 1.65 1.56 After issuance of the 481,667 shares resulting from the full conversion 1.61 1.53 Based on the 15,843,148 shares outstanding and the consolidated equity as of December 31, 2025 (i.e. €19,131,415), the theoretical impact on equity per share would be: On a non-diluted basis On a diluted basis 1 Before full conversion of the notes 1.21 1.15 After issuance of the 481,667 shares resulting from the full conversion 1.19 1.13 Based on 15,825,248 shares existing before conversion, the impact of the full conversion of the bonds on a shareholder holding 1% of the Company's share capital would be as follows: On a non-diluted basis On a diluted basis 1 Before full conversion of the notes 1.00 0.95 After issuance of the 481,667 shares resulting from the full conversion 0.97 0.92 1 Dilution takes into account the exercise of all outstanding dilutive instruments likely to result in the issuance of a maximum indicative number of 897,043 new shares (including the issuance of 500,000 related to the completion of the acquisition of Hospitex International). 2026 outlook: pursuit of industrial and commercial rollout of the integrated oncology diagnostics platform Building on the momentum achieved in 2025, the Company intends to continue the industrial and commercial rollout of its integrated oncology diagnostics platform, which combines standardized sample preparation, liquid-based cytology, automated FISH analysis, digital imaging, software, consumables and related services. This momentum is supported, in particular, by several key milestones achieved in 2025 and 2026, including the launch of Urine24, the exclusive distribution agreement signed with Menarini Diagnostics, the MoU signed with Cellay for the US market and the MoU signed with BioBrasil to produce its own FISH reagents and the two-distribution agreement signed in July 2026 for Romania and Saudi Arabia. Schedule for the Annual General Meeting The Company has obtained an extension from the Court to hold its Annual General Meeting by October 30, 2026. The final date and the meeting notice documents will be published in the Bulletin des Annonces Légales Obligatoires (BALO) and made available on the Company's website within the applicable legal deadlines. About ALIKO SCIENTIFIC Headquartered in Paris, ALIKO SCIENTIFIC is the parent company of an international ecosystem of businesses dedicated to advancing oncology diagnostics. Listed on Euronext Growth Paris under the ticker ALIKO, the company coordinates industrial, financial and research activities through its subsidiaries: Ikonisys Inc. (USA) and Hospitex International (Italy). ALIKO SCIENTIFIC's mission is to innovate cancer diagnosis by uniting cutting-edge technologies, resources, and strategic investments to create a global center of excellence in oncology. For more information, visit: www.alikoscientific.com About IKONISYS Ikonisys is a global leader in automated diagnostics, specializing in fluorescence in situ hybridization (FISH) and circulating tumor cell (CTC) detection. Leveraging advanced artificial intelligence (AI) and a fully automated microscopy platform, Ikonisys provides unmatched precision, scalability, and efficiency in cancer diagnostics and treatment monitoring. Recognized as pioneer in automation for rare cell detection, Ikonisys is at the forefront of personalized medicine, empowering clinicians to deliver targeted therapies and improve patient outcomes. https://www.bbc.co.uk/news/articles/cm75.text: Image source, Getty Images By Brandon Drenon Published 7 hours ago Minnesota Representative Ilhan Omar has said she can no longer live in her Washington DC home after it was searched by federal agents last week, fearing her address has been exposed after the raid. "With the death threats that I deal with, it's not, it's no longer going to be feasible to be in that house and have my kids," she told MS Now , external . In Omar's first public interview since the pre-dawn search of her home, she detailed how Homeland Security Investigations agents seized over a dozen items, including cell phones and notebooks, as part of an investigation. The government has not said what crime Omar is accused of but that the raid was "part of an ongoing federal criminal investigation". The search follows multiple comments from officials that cast doubt on Omar's US citizenship, which she received in 2000 after her arrival from Kenya. More than a dozen subpoenas have also been issued to members of Omar's family, as part of the investigation, and it was reported that her personal computers and passport were among the items that were seized. Recalling the hourslong raid of her home with MS Now, Omar said: "It obviously did freak all of us out." Omar said agents began "pounding on the doors" of her home at around 06:00 EDT (11:00 BST) on 12 October, startling her and her husband, who were both in bed. "We were screaming," she said, as the couple ran downstairs to see what was happening, calling the incident "so bizarre". The Minnesota Democrat estimated that between15 to 25 agents encircled her home, all of whom she said "conducted themselves in a decent way". Agents presented Omar with a warrant at the door after she asked for one. She then watched from the couch as agents spent roughly five hours going from room to room, Omar said, leaving with a total of 17 items, including multiple cellphones, notebooks, and her husband's camera from the 1960s. The BBC contacted the Justice Department for comment after being referred by the DHS. Omar again criticised the government's investigation, suggesting that it was meant to be intimidating. Immediately following the raid last week, she posted a statement online where she called it "an outrageous abuse of power" and "weaponisation of federal law enforcement to target political enemies". Former President Barack Obama has also blasted the federal probe, saying in a lengthy statement that it was "so appalling" . Omar, who has represented Minnesota since 2018, has long been a target of President Donald Trump's, who has repeatedly suggested she "go back" to Somalia. He has denied any involvement in her investigation, saying it has "nothing to do with me". At an Ohio rally in October, Trump referred to the search of her home, saying: "I don't know what they're doing with it, but I can tell you this: she's a disaster." The congresswoman, however, rejected the president's response, arguing that "he's got everything to do with it". "You know, this goes back to 2019 when he was screaming about the fact that, you know, I, I need to be sent back, I need to be deported." https://www.latintimes.com/second-drone-.text: Russia's Drone War Claims Another Ship in Bulgaria's Black Sea — 11 Sailors Missing The Briefing: Eleven sailors remain missing after the Guinea-Bissau-flagged cargo ship HS Dignity sank in Bulgaria's Black Sea exclusive economic zone on Tuesday; five crew members were rescued alive. A second vessel, the Maltese-flagged Chelsea 3, was struck by three drones in the same overnight attack, but all 15 crew — seven Ukrainians and eight Azerbaijanis — were evacuated safely with no serious injuries. This is the second deadly drone strike on merchant shipping in Bulgarian waters in seven days, and it has drawn emergency responses from NATO, the European Union, and Ukraine, all pointing toward Moscow as responsible. Eleven sailors are missing and feared dead after drone strikes sank a cargo ship inside Bulgaria's Black Sea exclusive economic zone Tuesday morning — the second time in a single week that commercial shipping has been sent to the bottom of the sea in Bulgarian waters, a pattern that is reshaping risk calculations across Eastern Europe and pushing NATO toward urgent decisions about the defense of its maritime flank.Two Ships Struck in the Night; One Never ReturnsThe attacks unfolded in the early hours off Bulgaria's northern Black Sea coast. The Guinea-Bissau-flagged cargo ship HS Dignity was struck and sank in waters off the village of Krapets; five crew members were pulled from the sea, but 11 remain unaccounted for. What rescue crews found at the scene gave little cause for hope: one overturned lifeboat, three life rafts, and scattered debris from the ship's equipment drifting on the surface.The second vessel hit that night was the Chelsea 3, sailing under a Maltese flag. Struck by three drones, it did not sink. All 15 crew — seven Ukrainians and eight Azerbaijanis — were brought to safety, with none reporting serious injuries.Bulgaria Points the Finger at MoscowSofia stopped short of a direct accusation, but the diplomatic signal was impossible to miss. In a nationally televised address, Prime Minister Rumen Radev called the strikes "absolutely unacceptable — another attack in the immediate vicinity of Bulgarian territorial waters," and said the outcome of the attacks "benefits the Russian Federation." He then spoke by telephone with European Commission President Ursula von der Leyen and NATO Secretary General Mark Rutte, pressing both to help Bulgaria bolster its maritime and airspace surveillance capabilities.Russia's ambassador to Sofia, Eleonora Mitrofanova, met with Radev but brought no information from Moscow's defense ministry on the strikes. She declined to rule out that the attacks were "a provocation by a third party" — a characterization that Ukraine and Western officials were quick to dispute. Ukrainian Foreign Minister Andrii Sybiha said the attack once again exposed Moscow's systematic disregard for civilian lives at sea, and described the Black Sea as a global food security artery that Russia was deliberately turning into a weapon.Brussels and NATO RespondEuropean Commission President Ursula von der Leyen declared the Black Sea had become another theater of Russian escalation in the war against Ukraine and demanded that those responsible face accountability. NATO Secretary General Mark Rutte said the alliance would continue to adjust its military presence along the eastern flank as the threat evolves.Seven Days Earlier: The First Deadly Strike in Bulgarian WatersTuesday's attack came exactly one week after drone warfare first entered Bulgaria's exclusive economic zone. On October 6, sea and aerial drones struck two merchant ships roughly 70 nautical miles east of the coastal town of Byala. The Togo-flagged Alfa Watan sank, with nine Syrian sailors and one Egyptian crew member lost. The Palau-flagged grain carrier Able caught fire, but its 18 Turkish and Indian crew members were all successfully rescued. Bulgaria halted its search for the Alfa Watan's missing crew after rescuers found no survivors and no sign of life in the water. Radev called that attack "absolutely unacceptable" — the same phrase he would reach for again seven days later. Ukrainian President Volodymyr Zelenskyy, citing a joint naval inquiry with Bulgaria, attributed the October 6 strikes directly to Russia, a conclusion Radev declined to formally endorse.Before That: A Turkish Grain Ship Burns Off RomaniaThe pattern of attacks on neutral commercial shipping had begun even before Bulgaria's waters were targeted. The day before the October 6 Bulgarian strikes, a Turkish-owned cargo ship transporting Ukrainian grain to Italy was hit by a drone, caught fire, and sank in the Black Sea off the coast of Romania. Two crew members died and 11 others were rescued. Ukraine blamed that attack on Russia as well.A Sea in Flames — And No End in SightThe escalating strikes are part of a broader economic war that neither side shows any sign of ending. Turkey's Chamber of Maritime Commerce reported in September 2026 that 226 civilian and commercial vessels had been attacked in the Black Sea since the war began in February 2022, with the vast majority of incidents concentrated in the current year.Russia has systematically targeted Ukraine's Black Sea port infrastructure, pushing Ukrainian exports toward the Danube and toward coastal shipping lanes that run through Bulgarian and Romanian waters. Ukraine, in turn, has intensified its own drone campaign against Russian grain-exporting ships in the Black Sea and the Azov Sea. What began as a bilateral war between two nations has now drawn NATO's eastern maritime flank into the line of fire — forcing the alliance to defend its members' sovereign economic zones while global shippers, grain traders, and insurers scramble to reassess every Black Sea route they operate.
